Today’s M&A briefing — 15 deals, the strategies behind them · 19 November 2026

🔹 NEO Next+ Energy Upstream UK acquires EnQuest — $960m.

🔹 SPIE (multi-technical services for energy, industry) acquires Enprom (EPC engineering and construction of high-voltage power grids for transmission operators in Poland and Germany).

🔹 CONEX (customs declaration software) acquires traide AI (AI-powered automation of customs tariff classification and export control in ERPs, SAP, Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics).

🔹 Knowmad Mood (spanish technology consultancy listed on BME Growth) acquires Danwor (data & Analytics, enterprise planning).

🔹 Acciaieria Arvedi (italian steelmaker) finalizes the acquisition of ArcelorMittal CLN Distribuzione Italia (AMCLN) (distribution of carbon flat steel products via service centers in Italy, production and supply of these products).
The European Commission approved the transaction, concluding that it did not raise competition concerns given its limited impact on the markets concerned.

🔹 Milient Software (project management software) acquires YVI Application Family (IVY cloud-platform for integrated CRM).

🔹 DJH acquires Haslehursts.

🔹 Signiant (media content distribution and management technologies) acquires Ceivo (content intelligence enabling media organizations to discover, analyze, and act on their assets, searching for phrases or visual elements).

🔹 SPG (Specific-Group) (IT services for modernizing core systems for banks) acquires ORBIT Cloud Solutions (cloud migration and operations).

🔹 Wallaby S.p.A (scagliarini family office) finalizes the acquisition of the 50% stake in BPB Medica (Biopsybell S.r.l.) not yet owned (design, production, and marketing of medical devices for minimally invasive surgery, biopsy, diagnosis, spinal surgery).

🔹 Nova Marine Carriers acquires Terminal Nord (port terminal at the Port of Ravenna, Italy).

🔹 Bos Logistics (data-driven logistics, growth strategy) acquires Rijlaarsdam's air freight activities at Schiphol (air freight operated from Schiphol by Rijlaarsdam).

🔹 Manzanos Enterprises (multi-sector family holding based in Azagra) finalizes the acquisition of Art's Golf Cars (sales of new and used golf vehicles and carts).

🔹 La maison Pariès (via Muxu and Macaron) (basque artisanal confectionery and pastry) finalizes the acquisition of Antton chocolate factory (SAS Eliodor) (artisanal chocolate factory founded in 1993).

🔹 Paehler Rietberg (spirits producer based in Rietberg-Mastholte) takes over Westfälische Kornbrand-Brennerei Hessling (kornbrand distillery in Beckum, Westphalia).

en.text:
Today’s fundraising briefing — 5 deals, the strategies behind them · 19 November 2026

🔹 Payhawk (enterprise expense management platform integrating payment cards, budget controls, procurement, travel, reporting, and AI agents) — $280m · Series C.
Payhawk reaches a valuation of $2 billion and has raised over $515 million since its inception. The round is entirely equity-based. 77% of its customers reportedly use its AI agents daily, which perform administrative tasks instead of finance teams.
𝗢𝘂𝗿 𝘃𝗶𝗲𝘄: The presence of Goldman Sachs Growth Equity—which places tickets of this size in companies nearing an IPO or divestment—signals that Payhawk is entering a pre-liquidity capitalization phase, with a platform thesis rather than a simple SaaS.

🔹 Dcubed (release actuators, deployable systems, and off-the-shelf power solutions for the space industry, founded in Munich) — €27.2m · Series A+.
ARAQYS's first product, HALO, is an origami-folding radial solar panel using consumer silicon cells, aiming to reduce the cost of space power by one to two orders of magnitude.
𝗜𝗻𝘃𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗿𝘀: Warsaw Equity Group (WEG, lead investor); EIC Fund (European Innovation Council); HTGF Opportunity Fund; BayBG and Expansion (existing investors).
𝗢𝘂𝗿 𝘃𝗶𝗲𝘄: Dcubed bets that the standardization of space hardware—as electronic components have been on Earth—creates a volume market in orbital energy infrastructure where there was only custom-made, as constellations and industrial applications in orbit multiply.

🔹 Fairly (US marketplace for vacation rental management via local managers supported by a dynamic pricing platform) — $22.4m · Series A.
𝗨𝘀𝗲 𝗼𝗳 𝗳𝘂𝗻𝗱𝘀: Geographic expansion, growth of the local manager network, and embedded AI development.
𝗜𝗻𝘃𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗿𝘀: Oregon Venture Fund (lead investor); Elevate Capital Fund; Eric Breon (founder and CEO).
𝗢𝘂𝗿 𝘃𝗶𝗲𝘄: Fairly's bet is structural: large rental management platforms have optimized for scale at the expense of service quality perceived by owners and travelers.

🔹 Treat (medical consultation preparation software for private healthcare: symptom collection, insurance and employer coverage verification) — €3m · Seed.
Treat has over 20 pilot employers, including a group of 1,300 employees, and its first thousands of users. According to the company, 83% of cases are resolved during a first digital consultation. Data does not pass through public language models.
𝗨𝘀𝗲 𝗼𝗳 𝗳𝘂𝗻𝗱𝘀: Product development and international expansion, with a goal of more than five active countries before the end of the year.

🔹 Perry AI (legal operating system for private equity and venture capital funds: living memory of rights, obligations) — €2m · Seed.

Levées de fonds : les 5 opérations chiffrées de l'édito du 19 novembre 2026.

🔹 Payhawk (𝑝𝑙𝑎𝑡𝑒𝑓𝑜𝑟𝑚𝑒 𝑑𝑒 𝑔𝑒𝑠𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑑𝑒𝑠 𝑑𝑒́𝑝𝑒𝑛𝑠𝑒𝑠 𝑑'𝑒𝑛𝑡𝑟𝑒𝑝𝑟𝑖𝑠𝑒 𝑖𝑛𝑡𝑒́𝑔𝑟𝑎𝑛𝑡 𝑐𝑎𝑟𝑡𝑒𝑠 𝑑𝑒 𝑝𝑎𝑖𝑒𝑚𝑒𝑛𝑡, 𝑐𝑜𝑛𝑡𝑟𝑜̂𝑙𝑒𝑠 𝑏𝑢𝑑𝑔𝑒́𝑡𝑎𝑖𝑟𝑒𝑠, 𝑎𝑐ℎ𝑎𝑡𝑠, 𝑣𝑜𝑦𝑎𝑔𝑒𝑠) — 280 M$ · Série C.
Payhawk atteint une valorisation de 2 Md$ et a levé plus de 515 M$ depuis sa création. Le tour est entièrement en equity. 77 % de ses clients utiliseraient quotidiennement ses agents IA, qui exécutent les tâches administratives à la place des équipes finance.
𝗣𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁 𝗱𝗲 𝘃𝘂𝗲 : La présence de Goldman Sachs Growth Equity — qui place des tickets de cette taille dans des sociétés proches d'une introduction en bourse ou d'une cession — signale que Payhawk entre dans une phase de capitalisation pré-liquidity, avec une thèse de plateforme plutôt que de simple SaaS.

🔹 Dcubed (𝑎𝑐𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛𝑛𝑒𝑢𝑟𝑠 𝑑𝑒 𝑙𝑖𝑏𝑒́𝑟𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛, 𝑠𝑦𝑠𝑡𝑒̀𝑚𝑒𝑠 𝑑𝑒́𝑝𝑙𝑜𝑦𝑎𝑏𝑙𝑒𝑠 𝑒𝑡 𝑠𝑜𝑙𝑢𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛𝑠 𝑑'𝑎𝑙𝑖𝑚𝑒𝑛𝑡𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑒́𝑙𝑒𝑐𝑡𝑟𝑖𝑞𝑢𝑒 𝑠𝑢𝑟 𝑒́𝑡𝑎𝑔𝑒̀𝑟𝑒 𝑝𝑜𝑢𝑟 𝑙'𝑖𝑛𝑑𝑢𝑠𝑡𝑟𝑖𝑒 𝑠𝑝𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑎𝑙𝑒) — 27,2 M€ · Série A+.
Le premier produit ARAQYS, HALO, est un panneau solaire radial à pliage origami utilisant des cellules silicium grand public, visant à réduire le coût de la puissance spatiale d'un à deux ordres de grandeur.
𝗣𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁 𝗱𝗲 𝘃𝘂𝗲 : Dcubed parie que la standardisation du hardware spatial — comme les composants électroniques l'ont été sur Terre — crée un marché de volume dans l'infrastructure énergétique orbitale là où il n'y avait que du sur-mesure, à mesure que les constellations et les applications industrielles en orbite se multiplient.

🔹 Fairly (𝑚𝑎𝑟𝑘𝑒𝑡𝑝𝑙𝑎𝑐𝑒 𝑎𝑚𝑒́𝑟𝑖𝑐𝑎𝑖𝑛𝑒 𝑑𝑒 𝑔𝑒𝑠𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑑𝑒 𝑙𝑜𝑐𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛𝑠 𝑑𝑒 𝑣𝑎𝑐𝑎𝑛𝑐𝑒𝑠) — 22,4 M$ · Série A.
𝗢𝗯𝗷𝗲𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗳 : Expansion géographique, croissance du réseau de gestionnaires locaux et développement de l'IA embarquée.
𝗔𝘃𝗲𝗰 : Oregon Venture Fund (chef de file) ; Elevate Capital Fund ; Eric Breon (fondateur et CEO).
𝗣𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁 𝗱𝗲 𝘃𝘂𝗲 : Le pari de Fairly est structurel : les grandes plateformes de gestion locative ont optimisé pour l'échelle au détriment de la qualité de service perçue par les propriétaires et les voyageurs.

🔹 Treat (𝑙𝑜𝑔𝑖𝑐𝑖𝑒𝑙 𝑑𝑒 𝑝𝑟𝑒́𝑝𝑎𝑟𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑑𝑒 𝑐𝑜𝑛𝑠𝑢𝑙𝑡𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑚𝑒́𝑑𝑖𝑐𝑎𝑙𝑒 𝑒𝑛 𝑠𝑎𝑛𝑡𝑒́ 𝑝𝑟𝑖𝑣𝑒́𝑒 : 𝑟𝑒𝑐𝑢𝑒𝑖𝑙 𝑑𝑒𝑠 𝑠𝑦𝑚𝑝𝑡𝑜̂𝑚𝑒𝑠) — 3 M€ · Seed.

🔹 Perry AI (𝑠𝑦𝑠𝑡𝑒̀𝑚𝑒 𝑑'𝑒𝑥𝑝𝑙𝑜𝑖𝑡𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑗𝑢𝑟𝑖𝑑𝑖𝑞𝑢𝑒 𝑝𝑜𝑢𝑟 𝑓𝑜𝑛𝑑𝑠 𝑑𝑒 𝑝𝑟𝑖𝑣𝑎𝑡𝑒 𝑒𝑞𝑢𝑖𝑡𝑦 𝑒𝑡 𝑣𝑒𝑛𝑡𝑢𝑟𝑒 𝑐𝑎𝑝𝑖𝑡𝑎𝑙 : 𝑚𝑒́𝑚𝑜𝑖𝑟𝑒 𝑣𝑖𝑣𝑎𝑛𝑡𝑒 𝑑𝑒𝑠 𝑑𝑟𝑜𝑖𝑡𝑠) — 2 M€ · Seed.
